paper: Sadek et al. (2020) — First Genomic Characterization of blaVIM-1 and mcr-9-Coharbouring Enterobacter hormaechei Isolated from Food of Animal Origin
context: All 7 genomic claims independently reproduced from public NCBI data. The questions below are TRULY OPEN — not answered by the paper, not answerable from the deposited assembly alone, and directly grounded in the Enterobacter hormaechei / blaVIM-1 / mcr-9 co-carriage biology examined in this replication.

open_questions.q: Does the chromosomal QseBC two-component system in this MS37 isolate trans-activate the plasmid-borne mcr-9, or does the absence of a cis-linked plasmid qseBC pair genuinely leave mcr-9 transcriptionally silent under all physiological conditions?
open_questions.basis: The paper argues mcr-9 is 'silent' because pMS-37a carries mcr-9 but LACKS the downstream qseC/qseB regulatory pair — this is the core mechanistic hypothesis for the colistin-S phenotype (MIC 0.5 µg/mL). Our tblastn independently confirmed no qseB/qseC on pMS-37a (only a weak 27% paralog for qseC), BUT we also found bona-fide chromosomal copies (qseB 80.7% id 218 aa; qseC 69.5% id 449 aa on CP053190.1 near position 3.93 Mb). Whether those chromosomal QseBC copies can substitute in trans is neither addressed by the paper nor deducible from sequence.
next_steps: Recover the strain from the depositing lab / culture collection.
qRT-PCR of mcr-9 mRNA in wild-type MS37 vs. chromosomal qseBC deletion vs. plasmid-borne qseBC complementation, ±sub-MIC colistin, ±sub-MIC zinc (known QseBC trigger).
Broth microdilution colistin MIC across the same conditions to see whether trans-activation shifts MIC from S (0.5) toward R (≥4).

open_questions.q: Is the IS903 element upstream of mcr-9 on pMS-37a a novel IS903 sub-family variant, or one of the known IS903B/C/D lineages — and does the sub-family identity affect the likelihood of mcr-9 mobilisation?
open_questions.basis: Our BLAST identified an IS903 element at 87.6% id (not the 99.87% we got for IS1 downstream). IS903 is a variant family with sub-lineages (IS903B, C, D) from different Enterobacteriaceae, and no ISfinder canonical allele scored perfectly. The paper does NOT specify which IS903 sub-family it detected. Since IS-mediated mobilisation depends on transposase activity that varies across IS903 sub-families, the sub-family assignment matters for the paper's One-Health dissemination argument.
next_steps: Submit the 1,062 bp aligned IS903 region from pMS-37a (positions 136,074–137,131) to the ISfinder curator for formal sub-family classification.
Compare transposase amino-acid identity against IS903B/C/D reference proteins; test transposition frequency in a mate-out assay if the sub-family is novel.

open_questions.q: Is the specific IS903–mcr-9–IS1 + no-plasmid-qseBC architecture on pMS-37a a recurrent motif on IncHI2 plasmids carrying mcr-9 globally, or a one-off local Egyptian variant?
open_questions.basis: The paper reports this configuration for a single isolate. Multiple subsequent surveys (Kieffer 2019, Rozwandowicz 2018, Yuan 2019) have described IncHI2/mcr-9 plasmids with variable flanking-IS architectures and variable presence of qseBC downstream of mcr-9. Whether the specific 'IS903 up + IS1 down + no qseBC' triple co-occurs elsewhere — and whether it correlates with colistin susceptibility across isolates — determines whether MS37 is representative or a genomic curiosity.
next_steps: Assemble a pan-plasmid dataset of all NCBI-deposited IncHI2 replicons carrying mcr-9 (n≈150 as of 2024).
Annotate the 20 kb window centred on mcr-9 in each plasmid.
Cross-tabulate flanking-IS composition and qseBC presence/absence vs. reported colistin MIC where available.

open_questions.q: Can pMS-37a — carrying blaVIM-1 and mcr-9 on the same IncHI2 backbone — be conjugated between Enterobacterales at rates that make co-transfer of carbapenem + colistin resistance clinically plausible in a food-chain scenario?
open_questions.basis: The paper's One-Health framing rests on the implicit assumption that pMS-37a is transmissible. IncHI2 plasmids are generally conjugative, but conjugation frequency varies enormously with donor/recipient pair, temperature (IncHI2 has thermosensitive tra), and stress conditions. The paper does not report a filter/broth mating experiment. Without that datum, the food-chain-risk argument is genomically plausible but empirically undemonstrated.
next_steps: Perform filter mating from strain MS37 (or a rifampicin-resistant derivative) into E. coli J53 recipient at 26 °C, 30 °C, and 37 °C.
Select transconjugants on carbapenem + colistin (or carbapenem alone, then screen colistin phenotype).
PCR-verify both blaVIM-1 and mcr-9 on the same IncHI2 rep in transconjugants; measure transfer frequency.

open_questions.q: Under selective pressure (sub-MIC colistin, or acquisition of a functional cis qseBC via recombination), how quickly does the colistin-susceptible 'silent mcr-9' phenotype revert to a colistin-resistant one, and by what mechanism (regulatory rescue vs. IS-mediated qseBC acquisition vs. secondary mutations)?
open_questions.basis: The paper's 'silent mcr-9 could disseminate cryptically' warning is a rate hypothesis: it predicts that a silent-mcr-9 isolate can rapidly become resistant when placed under colistin selection. This is testable but has not been tested for MS37. Escape mechanisms could include (a) trans-activation by chromosomal QseBC upregulating in response to colistin, (b) IS-mediated capture of qseBC from a co-resident plasmid or the chromosome placing it in cis, or (c) secondary mutations bypassing the requirement for qseBC.
next_steps: Serial passage of MS37 in increasing sub-MIC colistin (0.25→8 µg/mL over 30–50 passages), in triplicate.
Whole-genome resequencing of any evolved colistin-R lineages to identify the genetic route (regulatory vs. IS-mediated vs. point mutation).
Measure mcr-9 mRNA levels in evolved vs. ancestral strains to confirm the resistance route is via mcr-9 activation and not an alternative colistin-R mechanism (mgrB, pmrA/B, etc.).
